regime_context: Broad, non-directional rotation across 16 Canada/TSX themes: 9 eligible under the absolute-trend gate, no crowding flags anywhere, and absorption is low (0.31). Gate discipline shows genuine drawdown-control value on this history (gate_helps=true), but cross-sectional momentum is a focus lens only and rotation timing has no forward edge; the dominant macro narrative is coincident and irrelevant as a trigger.
emerging_watch: Watching Oil & Gas Producers (rank 4, eligible, but breadth a thin 0.429 and Hurst 'mixed') for either confirmation of leadership broadening into energy or a fade back into the mean-revert crowd. The observable I want: Oil & Gas breadth rises above 0.6 while durability_bar holds at or above 0.55 for ten consecutive trading days. If instead XEG.TO breadth stays under 0.5 as the precious-metals bloc keeps leading, the energy handoff hypothesis retires.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners lead with the strongest durability bar (0.66), near-unanimous breadth (0.933), and eligibility confirmed by the only validated edge — the absolute-trend gate. The lens shows leadership concentration here, and the gate says the trend is intact enough to stay in rather than be shaken out. This is a stay-with-the-trend lean, not a return forecast.
theses.dissent: Hurst tag is 'mixed' rather than 'trend', and r10 is slightly negative (-0.0054); the precious-metals complex in Canada is highly sensitive to a single macro variable (gold price), which can reverse without warning and drag the whole breadth profile down.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO closes below its own 50-day moving average while Gold Miners' breadth drops below 0.7 before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties sits just behind the leader with a comparable profile (durability 0.63, breadth 0.917, eligible). It is the challenger in the rotation structure, and the margin between leader and challenger (0.173) is thin enough that this is effectively one precious-metals leadership bloc rather than two independent bets. Lean is to stay with the bloc while the gate holds.
theses.dissent: Silver & Royalties share the same proxy (XGD.TO) as Gold Miners, so this is not an independent theme — it is the same precious-metals exposure twice. If gold price stalls, both names decline together, and the 'challenger' label overstates diversification.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO underperforms the S&P/TSX benchmark by more than 4% while Silver & Royalties breadth falls below 0.6 before the check-by date

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the only top-half theme with a clean 'trend' Hurst tag and a solid durability bar (0.66), still eligible under the gate. Among financials it is the stronger, cleaner trend relative to Insurers and Asset Managers. The lens places it 5th, but the trend-health leg is what supports a modest stay-with-lean here.
evidence: hurst_tag: trend — rare among current leaders
theses.dissent: Breadth is weak (0.429) and the TSX financials complex is heavily rate-sensitive; a single policy surprise can hit all Big Banks simultaneously, and a 'trend' tag with thin breadth often marks the late stage of a move.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO gives back its 30-day gain and Big Banks' breadth falls to 0.25 or lower before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
